_comment: webCoRE-JSON signatures that FORCE the PyScript band (COMPILER_SPEC §3.2). YAML/classic is the default; these are the exceptions. Data-driven on purpose (COMPILER_DECISIONS_HOLDING §E1) - edit here, never in compiler code. Checked by shim/compiler/routing.py. cancelTasks was removed 2026-07-20: mode:restart already cancels this automation's pending delays when it retriggers, so the YAML band expresses it natively (as a no-op). piston_scope_commands moved here from command_maps.json 2026-07-26: it is ROUTING (which commands the YAML band cannot express, so they go to PyScript), not translation, and translation now lives solely in webcore_vocab.json.
_split_rules_comment: THE SPLIT RULE (COMPILER_SPEC 3.2b; HARD_RULES 10). A piston is ONE intent, but HA cannot always RUN one intent as one automation. These are the shapes HA structurally cannot hold in a single automation, so the compiler must break them out and then keep the pieces connected and in order. This is a MOVING line, exactly like the PyScript one above - HA gains abilities, and when it does you turn a rule off HERE instead of editing compiler code (HARD_RULES 3 + 8). Each rule: 'enabled' is the switch, 'becomes' is what the broken-out piece is emitted as, 'why' is the evidence so a later reader knows whether it still applies. Splitting is a CONSEQUENCE of what HA can run, never a style choice - never split a piston just because the pieces are easier to compile.

nested_subscription.why: webCoRE's `on <event> do` is a trigger sitting INSIDE the piston. HA triggers exist only at automation level - you cannot nest one in an action sequence. 'Do X every time Y happens' therefore requires its own automation (WEBCORE_HA_BEHAVIOR_MAP.md:98, 'webCoRE pistons are event-driven internally; HA automations are event-driven externally'). NOTE: 'on' also appears in statement_types above, which sends the whole piston to PyScript today. That entry is what this rule is meant to RETIRE once splitting is wired through the emitters - do not remove it until then, or `on` pistons will compile to something that never fires.

independent_timed_branches.why: webCoRE cancels pending work per CONDITION GROUP - each timed branch is its own independent cancel unit. HA's `mode: restart` cancels the ENTIRE automation run. Two timed branches sharing one automation therefore kill each other's pending waits, silently. COMPILER_SPEC 2.5 point 4 already worked this out: one automation per condition group is what makes mode:restart exact; bundling is what breaks it.

work_after_wait.why: In webCoRE a pending task goes to a scheduler and the piston carries on. In HA a `delay` STOPS its sequence - everything behind it is hostage until it elapses. Emitting the continuation as its own script lets the parent carry on, and is the only shape where a cancel can reach the pending work at all, because scripts are individually addressable via script.turn_off (COMPILER_TODO.md:335-350, decision B).

timer_backed_waits.why: A `delay:` cannot be cancelled from outside its own automation run, so `cancelTasks` could never reach pending work — PROVEN ON A DEVICE 2026-08-08: the cancel fired, was accepted, and the cancelled turn-off ran anyway. It only LOOKS fine on the common shape because the waiting automation usually shares the trigger that fired the cancel and `mode: restart` throws the delay away as a side effect; change the piston's cancellation policy so the mode becomes `queued` and the bug appears. An HA timer helper is a real entity, so `timer.cancel` reaches it from anywhere, and HA's own docs state it cancels WITHOUT firing the finished event - which is exactly what makes the continuation not run. Bench-verified both directions 2026-08-08.
timer_backed_waits._margin_why: The wait_for_trigger timeout is the backstop for a cancel: no finished event ever arrives, so the run must give up and stop rather than hang. The margin only has to outlast HA's own scheduling jitter.
timer_backed_waits._not_covered: waitForTime / waitForDateTime wait for an ABSOLUTE time, not a duration, so they are a different shape and still emit their own wait. They carry the same cancellation gap; listing them here without building that shape would be a silent claim to fix something that is not fixed.
